daily.title: Aluminium Makers Seek Duty-Free Imports Ahead of FY28 Budget
daily.summary: Manufacturers seek zero basic customs duty to support downstream industry The association said the existing levy, which becomes an effective import duty of 8.25 per cent after including the social welfare surcharge, creates a structural cost disadvantage for downstream manufacturers. The sector includes a large number of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), for which raw material costs account for a substantial share of overall manufacturing expenses. Primary aluminium prices in India are influenced by international prices and import-parity considerations, making customs duty an important component of the domestic price benchmark.

daily.title: ITAT Hyderabad: Pre-Amendment Section 14A Disallowance Cannot Exceed Exempt Income
daily.summary: ITAT Hyderabad caps Section 14A disallowance at Rs.56.79 lakh and holds that the Finance Act 2022 amendment cannot apply retrospectively to AY 2018-19. Can the Assessing Officer disallow ₹5.35 crore under Section 14A when the company earned only ₹56.79 lakh in exempt income ? In DCIT Vs My Home Constructions Private Limited, ITA No. 2352/HYD/2025 , decided on 20 November 2026 , the Hyderabad ITAT held that, under the law applicable to AY 2018–19 , the disallowance could not exceed the exempt income earned during the year.

daily.title: ITAT Hyderabad: Agricultural Land Status Requires Municipal Limits and Distance Verification
daily.summary: ITAT Hyderabad admits additional evidence and remands Rs.61 lakh agricultural land sale dispute for verification of municipal limits, population and distance. Can agricultural land be treated as a capital asset based on the population of an urban area without verifying where the land lay in relation to the relevant municipal limits? In Yeruva Vinod Kumar Reddy Vs ITO, ITA No. 2452/HYD/2025 , decided on 20 November 2026 for AY 2018–19 , the Hyderabad ITAT held that the issue required verification of the location of the land, the population of the relevant municipality and the distance from its limits .

breaking.title: Sebi Asks Intermediaries To Stop Publishing IPO Grey Market Premiums
breaking.summary: The regulator warned that such off-exchange trades carry no settlement guarantee or dispute redressal for investors. Markets regulator Sebi on Monday asked intermediaries and market participants to stop publishing unregulated pre-listing premium figures, commonly known as the grey market premium, for upcoming IPOs. The regulator also cautioned investors against treating the premium as an indicator of listing prices or returns. It said such transactions occur outside the exchange framework, carry no settlement guarantee and give investors no access to dispute redressal mechanisms such as the online dispute resolution portal. The advisory covers websites, email, SMS and social media.
